name: Wholesale Inquiry to Quote to Shopify Draft Order

parameters.content:
## 1. Receive the form
Your website form posts each inquiry here from its server, with the shared secret in the `X-Form-Secret` header. A wrong secret gets 401 and bad fields get 400. With no secret configured every post is refused with 500 and an alert goes out.

parameters.errorMessage: WHOLESALE_FORM_SECRET is not set, so every wholesale form post is refused with 500. Add it to the n8n environment and restart n8n.

parameters.content:
## 2. Skip repeats and load the catalog
The submission id becomes the quote's Inquiry ID. A repeat post of a quote that was emailed gets 200 with its number; a quote still in Draft (an earlier run stopped half way) is finished instead. Then the active products, price tiers and batches are read (every page), about 300 ms apart (Airtable allows 5 requests a second per base), and the Claude request is built from them. The form gets 202 only once all of that worked, and 503 if Airtable did not answer or the catalog is empty or cut short, so it can simply post again.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ status: 'duplicate', inquiryId: $('Code: Check Form').first().json.inquiry.inquiryId, quoteNumber: $json.records[0].fields['Quote Number'] }) }}
={{ JSON.stringify({ error: 'try_again', message: 'We could not take your request just now. Please try again in a minute.' }) }}

parameters.errorMessage: ={{ $json.problem ? $json.problem : 'Airtable did not answer' + ' for inquiry ' + $('Code: Check Form').first().json.inquiry.inquiryId + ' from ' + $('Code: Check Form').first().json.inquiry.email + ' (HTTP ' + (($json.error || {}).status || ($json.error || {}).statusCode || (($json.error || {}).response || {}).status || 'error') + '), so the form got a 503 and nothing was saved. The form can post again.' }}

parameters.content:
## 3. Read the message
Claude reads the free text through a forced tool call and can only pick SKUs from the catalog. If Claude is down, refuses or answers badly, a rule-based reader takes over and the quote goes to a person.

## 4. Price, check and save
Prices come from the Price List tiers, never from Claude. Stock and production lead time give the feasibility. The quote is upserted on Inquiry ID (as Draft), then its number is checked: if another quote saved the same number first, this one takes the next. The lines are upserted on Line Label, 10 per request and one request per pass of the loop, so each request gets its own retries. Running this stage again never duplicates anything, which is what the cooldown loop relies on: on a 429 it waits 31 seconds (Airtable blocks the base for 30) and tries again, at most twice.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ performUpsert: { fieldsToMergeOn: ['Inquiry ID'] }, records: [{ fields: $('Code: Price Quote').first().json.quoteFields }], typecast: false }) }}

parameters.errorMessage: ={{ 'The quote was not saved to Airtable' + ' for inquiry ' + $('Code: Check Form').first().json.inquiry.inquiryId + ' from ' + $('Code: Check Form').first().json.inquiry.email + ' (HTTP ' + (($json.error || {}).status || ($json.error || {}).statusCode || (($json.error || {}).response || {}).status || 'error') + '). The form already got a 202; post it again once Airtable answers (the quote keeps its number). ' + String(($json.error || {}).message || '').slice(0, 300) }}

parameters.content:
## 5. Email the buyer
A clean quote is emailed through Postmark and marked Sent. A quote that needs review gets an acknowledgement email, Status Needs Review and a Slack alert instead. The status write also links the quote to exactly the lines in this email. A failed email flags the quote and raises an alert.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ records: [{ id: $('Code: Build Quote Lines').first().json.quoteRecordId, fields: Object.assign({ 'Status': $('Code: Price Quote').first().json.finalStatus, 'Email Message ID': $json.MessageID, 'Quote Lines': $('Loop Over Line Batches').all().flatMap(i => (i.json.records || []).map(r => r.id)) }, $('Code: Price Quote').first().json.emailKind === 'quote' ? { 'Sent At': $now.toUTC().toISO() } : {}) }] }) }}

parameters.errorMessage: ={{ 'The ' + ($('Code: Price Quote').first().json.emailKind === 'quote' ? 'quote email' : 'acknowledgement email') + ' for ' + $('Code: Price Quote').first().json.quoteNumber + ' went to ' + $('Code: Price Quote').first().json.email + ', but Airtable was not updated (HTTP ' + (($json.error || {}).status || ($json.error || {}).statusCode || (($json.error || {}).response || {}).status || 'error') + '). Set its Status to ' + $('Code: Price Quote').first().json.finalStatus + ' by hand; until then a repost of the form sends the email again.' }}
={{ $('Code: Email Failed').first().json.alert + ($json.error ? ' Airtable could not be updated either.' : '') }}

parameters.content:
## 6. Every 15 minutes, or Run Now
The schedule and the Run Now webhook start the same check. Run Now needs the `X-Run-Now-Secret` header and answers 202 before the work starts.

## 7. Find approved quotes
Status Approved and Processed not ticked, every page. No approved quotes: the run ends without writing anything.

parameters.errorMessage: ={{ 'Could not read approved quotes or products from Airtable (HTTP ' + (($json.error || {}).status || ($json.error || {}).statusCode || (($json.error || {}).response || {}).status || 'error') + '). Nothing was converted; the next run tries again.' }}

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ text: $('Code: Summarize Run').first().json.slackText + ($json.error ? '\n(The Sync Log row could not be written.)' : '') }) }}

parameters.content:
## 8. One quote at a time, then the summary
First look for a Shopify draft order tagged `quote-<number>`, so nothing is created twice. Then draftOrderCreate and draftOrderInvoiceSend, and the draft order id and invoice URL go back to the quote with Processed ticked. A problem with the quote sends it to Needs Review; an API problem keeps it Approved for the next run. When every quote is done: one Sync Log row and one Slack summary.
